title: The feeder finds its rate
about: How much should the worms get? Too little and they starve, too much and the box turns (see "Overfed"). Worms do not say, but the box gets lighter as they eat: about 0.6 g for every gram eaten. The feeder reads the load cells, fits a line through a day of weights, and proposes one day's eating. You still fill the hopper and confirm.

steps.title: You: fill the hopper
steps.why: 3 kg of scraps: enough for the feeder to draw on for a week.

steps.title: Robot: a first, small portion
steps.why: The feeder has no weight history yet, so it says it is learning and proposes a small portion that is safe for any box.

steps.title: Two days of weighing
steps.why: The clock runs at 2 hours a second. The feeder takes the box's weight at every look. After six hours of readings it has a first rate; a day of them makes it steadier.

do.label: Run the clock: 2 hours a second

expect.say: the feeder's estimate: {v} g eaten a day

steps.title: How good is the estimate?
steps.why: Only a simulation can answer this: it knows what the worms really eat. A real box cannot be asked, which is why the feeder is tried here first.

expect.say: what they really eat: {v} g a day

steps.title: Robot: one day's food
steps.why: Now the proposal carries the feeder's amount, and its reason is written under it. The first food is long eaten, so this is a full day's portion.
